intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that split-hand/foot malformation-6 (SHFM6) is caused by homozygous mutation in the WNT10B gene (601906) on chromosome 12q13.

checks.claim: Split-hand/foot malformation-6 (SHFM6) is caused by homozygous mutation in the WNT10B gene.
checks.evidence_quote: a homozygous missense WNT10b mutation (p.R332W) in all affected individuals but the atypical case plus in an asymptomatic female
checks.explanation: The paper links homozygous WNT10b mutation to recessive SHFM. The label 'SHFM6' is standard nomenclature.

checks.claim: The WNT10B gene is located on chromosome 12q13.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified by homozygosity mapping a novel SHFM locus at 12q13.11-q13 with a maximum multipoint lod score of 5.47 and by subsequent candidate gene approach a homozygous missense WNT10b mutation
checks.explanation: WNT10b was found as the candidate gene in the 12q13 locus.

paragraphs.text: Split-hand/foot malformation (SHFM), or ectrodactyly, is a congenital limb malformation affecting the central rays of the hands and/or feet. It produces a median cleft, absent or hypoplastic central digits, and often syndactyly of the remaining digits. SHFM6 is the autosomal recessive form caused by mutation in WNT10B. Severity varies within families, and penetrance may be incomplete.

checks.claim: Split-hand/foot malformation (SHFM), also called ectrodactyly, is a congenital limb malformation affecting the central rays of the hands and/or feet.
checks.evidence_quote: Split hand and foot malformation syndrome (SHFM) is characterized by the absence of the central digital rays
checks.explanation: The abstract supports the central-ray involvement of the hands and feet. It does not use the term 'ectrodactyly' or say 'congenital' outright.

checks.claim: Split-hand/foot malformation produces a median cleft of the hands and/or feet.
checks.evidence_quote: absence of the central digital rays, deep median cleft, and syndactyly of the remaining digits
checks.explanation: The abstract names the deep median cleft as a defining feature.

checks.claim: Split-hand/foot malformation produces absent or hypoplastic central digits.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by the absence of the central digital rays
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions absent central rays but not hypoplastic ones.

checks.claim: Split-hand/foot malformation often includes syndactyly of the remaining digits.
checks.evidence_quote: deep median cleft, and syndactyly of the remaining digits
checks.explanation: The abstract lists syndactyly of the remaining digits as a defining feature. It does not say it occurs 'often'.

checks.claim: SHFM6 is the autosomal recessive form of split-hand/foot malformation caused by mutation in WNT10B.
checks.evidence_quote: This is the first reported WNT10b mutation on the pathogenesis of limb development and recessive mutation in SHFM.
checks.explanation: The paper describes autosomal recessive SHFM caused by a WNT10b mutation.

checks.claim: The severity of split-hand/foot malformation varies within families.
checks.evidence_quote: A variable intrafamilial expression of the malformation pattern is apparent.
checks.explanation: Variable expression within the family is stated directly.

checks.claim: The penetrance of split-hand/foot malformation may be incomplete.
checks.evidence_quote: all showing variable expressivity and reduced penetrance
checks.explanation: The abstract states that penetrance is reduced.

paragraphs.text: SHFM6 is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait. This was shown by reports of affected offspring of consanguineous parents and of homozygous WNT10B mutations. Ugur and Tolun (2008) described the inheritance in their family as complex, with variable expressivity.

checks.claim: SHFM6 is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait.
checks.evidence_quote: We studied a large consanguineous kindred afflicted with autosomal recessive SHFM.
checks.explanation: The abstract states autosomal recessive SHFM.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive inheritance of SHFM6 was shown by reports of affected offspring of consanguineous parents.
checks.evidence_quote: We studied a large consanguineous kindred afflicted with autosomal recessive SHFM.
checks.explanation: The paper reports a consanguineous family with recessive SHFM.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive inheritance of SHFM6 was shown by reports of homozygous WNT10B mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: a homozygous missense WNT10b mutation (p.R332W) in all affected individuals but the atypical case
checks.explanation: The paper reports a homozygous WNT10b mutation.

checks.claim: Ugur and Tolun (2008) described the inheritance of SHFM in their family as complex.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygous WNT10b mutation and complex inheritance in Split-Hand/Foot Malformation.
checks.explanation: The title describes the inheritance as complex.

checks.claim: Ugur and Tolun (2008) described variable expressivity of SHFM in their family.
checks.evidence_quote: Twelve affected members had central feet reductions with or without hand involvement while the remaining one had the mildest phenotype and atypical SHFM.
checks.explanation: Variable phenotypes are described, but the abstract does not use the term 'variable expressivity'.

paragraphs.text: Ugur and Tolun (2008) studied a consanguineous Turkish family with autosomal recessive SHFM. They mapped the disorder to chromosome 12q13 by homozygosity mapping.

checks.claim: Ugur and Tolun (2008) studied a consanguineous Turkish family with autosomal recessive split-hand/foot malformation.
checks.evidence_quote: We studied a large consanguineous kindred afflicted with autosomal recessive SHFM.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not state that the family is Turkish.

checks.claim: Ugur and Tolun (2008) mapped autosomal recessive split-hand/foot malformation in a consanguineous Turkish family to chromosome 12q13 by homozygosity mapping.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified by homozygosity mapping a novel SHFM locus at 12q13.11-q13 with a maximum multipoint lod score of 5.47
checks.explanation: Mapping to 12q13 by homozygosity mapping is supported. The family's Turkish origin is not stated in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: SHFM is genetically heterogeneous. Other forms are inherited in an autosomal dominant or X-linked manner, and the autosomal recessive form described here results from mutation in WNT10B.

checks.claim: Split-hand/foot malformation is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: genetic heterogeneity, with at least five loci identified to date
checks.explanation: The abstract states that SHFM is genetically heterogeneous.

checks.claim: Some forms of split-hand/foot malformation are inherited in an autosomal dominant manner.
checks.evidence_quote: The majority of the familial cases are inherited in an autosomal dominant manner.
checks.explanation: Autosomal dominant inheritance is stated directly.

checks.claim: Some forms of split-hand/foot malformation are inherited in an X-linked manner.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 11 cited papers. The abstract doesn't mention X-linked inheritance.

checks.claim: The autosomal recessive form of split-hand/foot malformation SHFM6 results from mutation in WNT10B.
checks.evidence_quote: This is the first reported WNT10b mutation on the pathogenesis of limb development and recessive mutation in SHFM.
checks.explanation: Recessive SHFM is attributed to WNT10b mutation.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of the consanguineous Turkish family they had mapped to 12q13, Ugur and Tolun (2008) found a homozygous mutation in the WNT10B gene.

checks.claim: Ugur and Tolun (2008) found a homozygous mutation in the WNT10B gene in affected members of the consanguineous Turkish family with split-hand/foot malformation mapped to 12q13.
checks.evidence_quote: a homozygous missense WNT10b mutation (p.R332W) in all affected individuals but the atypical case plus in an asymptomatic female
checks.explanation: The homozygous WNT10b mutation is supported. However, the abstract does not state the family is Turkish, and the atypical affected individual did not carry the mutation (while an unaffected female did).

paragraphs.text: Blattner et al. (2010) reported a homozygous nonsense mutation in WNT10B in a patient with apparently sporadic SHFM, consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: Blattner et al. (2010) reported a homozygous nonsense mutation in WNT10B in a patient with apparently sporadic split-hand/foot malformation.
checks.evidence_quote: By examining WNT10B in a patient with sporadic SHFM, we identified a homozygous 4-bp duplication resulting in a premature termination codon.
checks.explanation: The title calls it a nonsense mutation, and the abstract describes a homozygous premature-termination variant in a sporadic patient.

checks.claim: The homozygous WNT10B nonsense mutation in the patient with apparently sporadic split-hand/foot malformation reported by Blattner et al. (2010) is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: Nine heterozygous relatives show no sign of SHFM. These findings have profound implications for genetic counseling. Obviously, sporadic SHFM may show recessive rather than dominant inheritance
checks.explanation: Recessive inheritance is concluded.

references.label: Blattner et al. (2010)
references.citation: Blattner A, Huber AR, Röthlisberger B. Homozygous nonsense mutation in WNT10B and sporadic split-hand/foot malformation (SHFM) with autosomal recessive inheritance. Am J Med Genet A 152A: 2053-6, 2010. [PubMed: 20635353]

references.label: Ugur and Tolun (2008)
references.citation: Ugur SA, Tolun A. Homozygous WNT10b mutation and complex inheritance in Split-Hand/Foot Malformation. Hum Mol Genet 17: 2644-53, 2008. [PubMed: 18515319]
